problems: Frame 10: The punchline doesn't match the picture. Floey says the last line, "That's 41, Maya", but the shot is a Maya close-up and Floey isn't in it. The script calls for a wide shot with Floey on the mug turning her head, giving a dry chip, then saying the line. Viewers hear the payoff with no speaker on screen, so the button falls flat on the shot that matters most.

Frame 10: Maya's acting is wrong for the button. She has a relaxed, smug half-smile with her arms down. The script calls for her to look caught, in the crossed pose, looking at the camera. Without the 'caught' reaction the ending doesn't land.
Frame 03: "Says who?" uses the crossed-arms pose. The script asks for the shrug pose with palms open and eyebrows raised. Using crossed arms here also spends the pose meant for the ending.

Frame 06: The source card is not on the laptop screen. Maya's typing and search aren't shown; a floating card covers her face instead. The line she's reading, 'Crawling can take… days to weeks', has no highlight ring; that row is the dimmer, greyed one, so the eye goes to the wrong line. The card also repeats almost word for word the sentence she's saying, which is already in the caption. That comes close to the 'never put the spoken sentence on screen as a text card' rule. Show it as her browser page with the ring on the right line.
Frame 07: On 'weeks' the scripted glasses slip doesn't happen; a purple '?' appears by the window instead. Small, but the reaction beat is missing.

Frame 09: On "Just one" Maya is looking down at the trackpad. The script has her look at the camera and mutter without looking down, then sneak the click. As drawn, the relapse doesn't read as a conspiratorial look to the viewer.

Frame 02: In the wide shot Floey is small, about a sixth of the frame width, down in the corner. On a phone her teasing head tilt and sip will be hard to see. Frame tighter, or make her bigger in the wide shots.
